faq.title: How it Works & FAQ
faq.subtitle: Everything you need to know about SoroWill, the trustless on-chain inheritance protocol for Stellar.

lifecycle.heading: The Full Lifecycle
lifecycle.description: Here's how your will progresses from creation to resolution:

create.title: Create a Will
create.description: Connect your wallet, deposit USDC, specify beneficiaries with percentage splits, set check-in and grace periods, and optionally add guardians. Your will is now active and locked on-chain.

checkins.title: Regular Check-ins
checkins.description: Before each check-in deadline (30, 60, 90, 180, or 365 days), you must prove you are still active by clicking the check-in button. This resets the deadline. You can update beneficiaries or settings at any time while active.

miss.title: Miss a Check-in
miss.description: If you do not check in by the deadline, anyone can trigger the grace period. Your beneficiaries are notified. You still have time to respond—just check in and the will remains active.

grace.title: Grace Period
grace.description: A grace period (3, 7, or 14 days) begins. If you check in during this time, your will remains active. If you do not respond, the grace period expires and funds are released.

release.title: Funds Released
release.description: Once the grace period expires, the contract automatically distributes your USDC to your beneficiaries according to the percentages you set. Beneficiaries can then claim their share.

items.question: How does SoroWill work?
items.answer: SoroWill is a smart contract on Stellar Soroban that automates inheritance. You lock USDC into the contract, specify beneficiaries and check-in periods, and prove you are still active by checking in before each deadline. If you miss a check-in, anyone can trigger the grace period. If the grace period passes without a response from you, the contract automatically distributes your funds to your beneficiaries according to the percentages you set.

items.question: What happens if I miss a check-in?
items.answer: If you miss a check-in deadline, anyone can trigger a grace period (which you set during creation, typically 3-14 days). During this grace period, you can still respond and prevent the release. You simply need to access SoroWill and check in again. If you do not respond before the grace period ends, the funds are released to your beneficiaries automatically.

items.question: Can I update my beneficiaries after creating a will?
items.answer: Yes, while you are active (before a check-in is missed), you can update your will with new beneficiaries, adjust percentages, or change your check-in and grace period settings. This is done by creating a new will with cloned settings and canceling the old one.

items.question: Can I cancel my will?
items.answer: Yes, at any time while you remain active (before the grace period is triggered), you can cancel your will and recover your funds. This is done through the will details page. Once a grace period is triggered, cancellation is no longer possible.

items.question: What are guardians and what can they do?
items.answer: Guardians are optional trusted addresses (up to 3) that you can designate. Any 2 guardians can force an early release of your will if you become incapacitated. This is an additional safeguard to ensure funds reach your beneficiaries if you cannot respond.

items.question: Can I recover my funds if I trigger a grace period?
items.answer: Yes, during the grace period (which you set when creating your will), you can still check in and prevent the release. Once the grace period expires without a check-in, the funds are released permanently and cannot be recovered.

items.question: What tokens does SoroWill support?
items.answer: SoroWill currently supports USDC on Stellar. You specify the token contract address when creating a will. Make sure you use the correct contract address for your network (testnet vs. mainnet).

items.question: Is SoroWill trustless?
items.answer: Yes. SoroWill is trustless because it is governed entirely by the smart contract. No lawyers, courts, or intermediaries are involved. The contract enforces the outcome exactly as you configured it. All logic is on-chain and transparent.

items.question: Can I see other wills or access someone else's will?
items.answer: No. Will details are private and can only be viewed by the will owner using their connected wallet. Beneficiaries and guardians can view their relevant information through dedicated pages.

items.question: What happens if I lose access to my wallet?
items.answer: If you lose access to your wallet and cannot check in, the grace period will eventually expire and your beneficiaries will receive the funds. If you designated guardians, any 2 of them can trigger an early release. SoroWill is designed to ensure funds reach your beneficiaries even if you cannot respond.

items.question: Can beneficiaries check their inheritance status?
items.answer: Yes. Beneficiaries can view the status of wills they are named in by using the share verification page. They can see the amount, beneficiary split, and current check-in status.

items.question: How do I know my will is safe?
items.answer: All wills are stored on the Stellar blockchain and secured by the SoroWill smart contract. Your private keys remain under your control. Only the will data is on-chain; your beneficiary addresses and settings are transparent but not reversible once submitted.

items.question: Can I use federated addresses?
items.answer: Yes. SoroWill supports Stellar federated addresses in the format name*domain.com for beneficiaries and guardians. Simply enter the federated address and use the Resolve button to convert it to the underlying Stellar address for confirmation.

items.question: What if I forget my check-in deadline?
items.answer: You set your own check-in period when creating a will (30, 60, 90, 180, or 365 days). We recommend setting calendar reminders for yourself. The will details page always shows your next check-in deadline.

items.question: Are there any fees?
items.answer: SoroWill does not take a percentage of your funds. You only pay standard Stellar network fees for transactions (check-in, creation, claim, etc.). These fees are typically very small.

items.question: How do I claim my inheritance?
items.answer: If you are a beneficiary of a will that has been released, you can claim your share through the inheritance page. You will need your Stellar wallet connected and must complete a simple transaction to receive your funds.

glossary.heading: Glossary of terms
glossary.description: Plain-language definitions for the terms you will meet in SoroWill.

will.definition: A smart contract holding your USDC with instructions for who receives it and when.

beneficiary.definition: A Stellar address that receives a percentage of the locked funds when the will is released.

basisPoints.definition: Hundredths of a percent. 10,000 basis points is 100%, so beneficiary shares must add up to 10,000.

checkIn.definition: A transaction proving you are still active. It resets your deadline.

gracePeriod.definition: The window after a missed check-in during which you can still respond before funds are released.

guardian.definition: A trusted address that can trigger an early release, typically two of them together.

federatedAddress.definition: A human-readable Stellar address such as name*domain.com that resolves to a Stellar account.

usdc.definition: A US dollar stablecoin on Stellar. SoroWill locks USDC only.

soroban.definition: Stellar's smart contract platform, which runs the SoroWill contract.
